case_name: Deoki Panjhiyara vs Shahshi Bhushan Narayan Azad & Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: Shashi Bhushan Narayan Azad & Anr — husband

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Appellant, married to respondent in 2006, filed petition under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 seeking reliefs including damages and maintenance. Interim maintenance granted by trial court at rate of Rs.2000/- per month.

legal_principles.principle: The legislative intent to include women, living in marriages subsequently found to be illegal or even in relationships resembling a marriage, within the protective umbrella of the DV Act is absolutely clear and must be given its full effect.
legal_principles.held: Learned counsel has urged that having regard to the above even if the marriage of the appellant and the respondent was void on account of the previous marriage of the appellant, the said fact, by itself, will not disentitle the appellant to seek maintenance and other reliefs under the DV Act, 2005.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 — Section 2

legal_principles.principle: A relationship in the nature of marriage is akin to a common law marriage which requires proof of the fact that parties had lived together in a shared household as defined in Section 2(s) of the DV Act, and satisfaction of certain conditions.
legal_principles.held: This court had occasion to consider the provisions of Section 2(f) of the DV Act to come to the conclusion that a relationship in the nature of marriage is akin to a common law marriage which requires, in addition to proof of the fact that parties had lived together in a shared household as defined in Section 2(s) of the DV Act, the following conditions to be satisfied: ...

outcome.final_order: Appellant's petition under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 allowed.
